subject: Post-demo: model slate scenarios, cost/latency & regression guardrails
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Malhotra <tim@brightwave.ai>; Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: model slate scenarios, cost/latency & regression guardrails

Hi Tim — thanks again for the time yesterday. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our demo focused on BrightWave's production goals (low-latency customer responses for conversational flows + strict cost target for inference). I put the recommended slate and rationale below and attached the benchmark CSV and prompt pack used during the session.

TL;DR recommended slate (tradeoffs summarized):
- redwood-m-7b-quant (8-bit): best cost baseline, good 95% latency, lower quality on long-context summarization (recommended for high-throughput notification generation).
- redwood-l-13b-fp16 (server optimized): balanced quality/latency; p50 ~55ms, p99 ~240ms in our dedicated profile — recommended for chat and assistant paths.
- redwood-xl-70b-clamp (mixed precision + KV-cache): top quality on long-form synthesis and multi-turn context, higher cost and p99 tail; keep as escalation model for rare long-horizon queries.

Why this mix: the 13B variant hits your quality bar on the 10 prompt test questions we walked through while keeping median latency within your SLA and maintaining acceptable costs. The 7B quantized engine is a cost-saver for stateless tasks. The 70B is an explicit fallback for complex multi-turn threads where hallucination risk is highest.

Operational safeguards we propose:
- routing policy: default to 13B; route to 7B for short templates (<=128 tokens) and to 70B only when a quality flag triggers (score < threshold or user opts-in).
- KV prefix caching: enable for conversational sessions to cut token work on multi-turns (expected 20–35% token cost reduction on your traffic shape).
- quantization profiles: ship with 7B-8bit and 13B-4bit experimental configs; include regression gates (see evaluation plan below) before enabling 4-bit in production.

Quality/regression plan (short):
- baseline eval: run the prompt_pack_brightwave_v2.md set nightly for two weeks under both 13B and 7B configs; collect Rouge/EM and custom quality checks.
- canary & rollback: 10% traffic canary on any quantized rollout with automatic rollback on quality delta > 3% on monitored metrics.
- alerting: regression alerts to your SRE + our CS team; include sample prompts and outputs for triage.

Next steps / owners:
1) BrightWave: share a small additional prompt sample set (10–15 examples of worst-case long dialogs) — Tim (by Wed 11/25)
2) Redwood: run the two-week nightly eval and share a dashboard and csv — Naomi (start Mon 11/23)
3) Ops: prepare routing policy config for your Dedicated pool; include cost control knobs — Monica (draft by Fri 11/27)
4) Commercial: outline committed-capacity uplift to keep p99 targets under high load — Ben (proposal by Tue 11/30)

Attachments: brightwave_benchmarks_v1.csv (benchmark results from demo runs), prompt_pack_brightwave_v2.md (eval prompts), demo_recording_20261121.mp4.

If that plan looks good, we can schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to lock the canary window and procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0183

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Tim Malhotra <tim@brightwave.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model slate scenarios, cost/latency & regression guardrails

Thanks Naomi — solid summary. Two quick commercial notes:
- Cost ballpark: 13B-fp16 (hosted/dedicated) ~ $650 / 1M tokens served (in your observed mix) vs 7B-8bit ~ $180 / 1M tokens; 70B escalation ~ $2,400 / 1M tokens. I will put together a simple scenario table for expected monthly spend based on the three routing profiles.
- Dedicated uplift: for the p99 guarantees under your target QPS, a reserved pool looks necessary to avoid cross-tenant interference; I will map that to three commit tiers.

I'll own the commercial scenario doc and send a proposal in the HubSpot deal by Tue. Monica / Naomi — please flag anything about the routing or KV caching constraints I should fold into the commercial doc.

-Ben
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Tim Malhotra <tim@brightwave.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model slate scenarios, cost/latency & regression guardrails

Naomi / team — appreciate the thorough recap. A few clarifying points from BrightWave's side:
1) The 70B fallback is fine but we need a hard monthly cost cap for escalation (we estimate only ~1% of traffic should hit it).
2) Can you share the specific regression metrics you plan to track? We have internal success metrics that value factuality highly (precision on entity extraction).
3) Procurement: can you confirm lead time for Dedicated pool (GPU types) and if we can start with a 30-day trial?

We will collate the long-dialog examples and share the file by Wed as requested. If you can get the nightly eval dashboard up early next week that would be great — we'll use it to prioritize the prompts we share.

Thanks,
Tim Malhotra
Director, Product AI | BrightWave

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Tim Malhotra <tim@brightwave.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model slate scenarios, cost/latency & regression guardrails

Tim — quick answers inline and next steps: 

1) 70B cap: we can implement a hard spend cap at routing layer and configure a fallback to 13B once the cap is reached. We'll include that in the routing config draft.

2) Regression metrics: we'll track (a) entity precision/recall on your labeled set, (b) hallucination score from our QA prompts (string-level mismatch), (c) response latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), and (d) token cost per response. We'll share the exact schema for each metric in the dashboard link by EOD Mon.

3) Dedicated lead time & trial: Typical lead time for provisioning a dedicated GPU pool (A2-equivalent nodes) is ~10 business days; we can offer a 30-day pilot on a small pool (trial terms in HubSpot doc). Ben will attach the commit tiers.

Action items recap:
- BrightWave: share long-dialog prompt samples (Tim by Wed 11/25)
- Redwood: nightly eval kickoff (Naomi Monday 11/23), commercial proposal in HubSpot (Ben by Tue 11/30), routing draft (Monica by Fri 11/27)

I'll circulate the dashboard link and the metric schema shortly.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to jump on a 30-min sync after you share prompts.

—Monica
Lead, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
